evals.name: azure-smart-tier-from-blog
evals.prompt: using context7 or microsoft docs create a entirely local documentation about: https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/optimize-object-storage-costs-automatically-with-smart-tier-now-generally-available/
evals.expected_output: A self-contained markdown doc on Azure Blob Storage smart tier: mechanics (30/90 day thresholds, 128 KiB small-object rule, Get/Put as access ops), prerequisites (GPv2 + ZRS/GZRS/RA-GZRS, block blobs only), the billing table, the SmartHot/SmartCool/SmartCold metric values, per-tool enablement with the 2025-08-01 api-version, and the lifecycle-management comparison. Sources cited with retrieval date.
assertions: States both tiering thresholds correctly: hot to cool after 30 days of no access, cool to cold after 60 more days (90 total)
Documents the 128 KiB small-object rule: objects below that size stay on hot and are not charged the monitoring fee
Contains a billing breakdown showing that tier transitions within smart tier, early deletion, and data retrieval are NOT charged
Lists all three prerequisites: Standard GPv2 (not GPv1 or premium), zone-redundant storage (ZRS/GZRS/RA-GZRS), and block blobs only
Includes a runnable enablement command quoting the 2025-08-01 API version
Names the smart-tier-specific metric values used for monitoring (SmartHot, SmartCool, SmartCold, SmartHot-small)
Distinguishes access operations that reset the timer (Get Blob, Put Blob) from those that do not (Get Blob Properties, Metadata, Tags)
Documents the one-way door: once an object is set to an explicit tier it cannot be returned to smart tier
Cites its sources with a retrieval date

evals.name: azurerm-v5-breaking-changes-at-pin
evals.prompt: azurerm just went to 5.x and we're still pinned at ~> 4.73 in iac/. can you write up a doc in docs/ covering what actually breaks for us, from https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/releases/tag/v5.0.0 — needs to be something i can hand to the team without them having to read the whole changelog
evals.expected_output: A doc scoped to THIS repo's pin: reads iac/*/versions.tf to find ~> 4.73, identifies which v5.0.0 breaking changes touch resources actually used in iac/ (azurerm_consumption_budget_*, azurerm_policy_*), and verifies claims against released artifacts rather than paraphrasing the changelog. Explicitly separates 'affects us' from 'does not affect us'.
assertions: Reads the repo's actual provider pin from iac/*/versions.tf and states it (~> 4.73)
Names the specific azurerm resources actually used in iac/ (consumption budget and/or policy resources) rather than discussing the provider generically
Scopes the breaking changes to what touches this repo instead of reproducing the full changelog
Explicitly separates changes that affect this repo from changes that do not
Verifies at least one claim against a released artifact at a version tag (raw source file, provider docs at tag, registry metadata) rather than relying only on the release notes
Cites its sources with a retrieval date
Does not assert the upgrade is safe or breaking-change-free without supporting evidence

evals.name: storage-actions-no-announcement
evals.prompt: add a doc for azure storage actions — we keep debating it vs lifecycle policies for the finops work and nobody remembers which does what. should live in docs/
evals.expected_output: A decision-oriented doc built from canonical Learn pages (no announcement URL was given): what Storage Actions is, its cost model vs lifecycle management's free-but-limited model, a comparison table covering predicates/deployment/monitoring, and a clear 'use X when' guide. Should match the repo's docs house style.
assertions: Sources content from canonical learn.microsoft.com pages rather than a blog post or announcement
Contains a comparison table covering Storage Actions vs lifecycle management across at least deployment model, cost, and targeting/predicates
States the cost difference correctly: lifecycle management has no service charge while Storage Actions carries a service fee
Gives a concrete decision guide saying when to pick each option
Mentions smart tier as the third option in the same cost-optimization decision space
Cites its sources with a retrieval date
Matches the destination repo's docs house style (heading structure and table usage consistent with sibling files in docs/)
